Li Hua: You should go out more. I'm meeting some friends for coffee now. Why don't you come?

Li Hua:

Wang Jun: Um. I went to Liu Ming's birthday party four weeks ago.

Wang Jun: No. I don't really enjoy it. I get nervous.

Li Hua:

We're going for dinner. How about joining us?

Questions 11-15 are based on the following passage.
Diamond is the hardest material on Earth. Yet, gem cutters shape them. If diamonds are so hard, how do they cut them into shape? They use other diamonds of course!
Not all diamonds are the same. Some are harder than others. The hardness of a diamond depends on two things: its purity and its structure. Let's discuss purity first.
Diamonds come in many colors: grey, white, yellow, blue, pink, purple, orange and black.
Red diamonds are the rarest of all. This makes them worth a lot of money. Yet, pure diamonds are colorless. They are all carbon. They are transparent like glass.

Colors found in diamonds come from impurities. They have another element besides carbon. They have a carbon defect. For example, yellow diamonds have nitrogen in them. The nitrogen is yellow. Blue diamonds have boron trapped in their crystal structure. The boron is blue.
The purity or color of a diamond is important to its hardness. Pure diamonds are harder than impure diamonds. But purity isn't the only thing that matters. Structure also affects hardness.

The carbon atoms in a diamond are arranged in a crystal structure. Some crystal structures are perfect. A diamond with a perfect crystal structure is harder than one with flaws. So pure, colorless crystal diamonds are the hardest of all.

Good gemstones should be hard. This is what makes diamonds so great for jewelry. Some gems, such as azurite, are soft and easy to scratch. Azurite looks pretty, but it will scratch if worn daily. Diamonds do not scratch easily. Only a diamond can scratch another diamond.
That's why you can wear a diamond ring while doing chores, if you want. The gem will not need polishing. Just don't go fist bumping other people with fancy engagement rings. It will end badly.
What are the two factors that determine a diamond's hardness according to the passage?
第二段直接指出 diamond 的 hardness depends on its purity and its structure。
C. Purity and structure.

Directions: Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are 4 choices marked A, B, C and D. Choose the ONE that best fits into the statement.
Questions 16-20 are based on the following passage.

Imagine that you get an email one morning. You click the link in the email. It takes you to a site that looks very much like your bank's. You enter your username and password. You submit the form. You've just been phished!

Phishing is a type of attack that happens over the Internet. Users receive an email or text message that seems like it came from a trusted source. These users are being cheated. They are interacting with dangerous hackers. The attackers copy trusted companies. They send users to web pages that look like the ones we use every day. When users login or provide sensitive information, the attackers steal this data.

Attackers want your data for many reasons. They may use your data to commit identity fraud. This is when they use your identity to buy something with your credit. Then they receive the goods and you receive the bill. Or they may want your password to take over a computer network. They may want access to private emails. They may want customer records. They gain access by tricking people into giving them their login information.

Phishing attacks are dangerous, but you can spot them if you pay attention. One thing to watch is your address bar in your browser. Attackers use domains that look like the ones that we trust, but they are not the same. If you are unsure, search for the site and login from the root domain.

An even better way to secure your account against phishing attacks is to use 2FA: two factor authentication. 2FA means that your account is secured with two keys. The first is your password. The second key is a random code that changes every few minutes.

Phishing attacks are scary and common. The reason why they are common is that they are effective. Many people accept appearances with no doubt. Browsing the Internet safely requires a healthy amount of suspicion. Nobody is trying to give you free money.
How do phishing attackers obtain users' data?

choices.label: A. When users receive an email from the attackers.
B. When users are interested in the web pages.
C. When users login or provide sensitive information.
D. When users click the link in an email from the attackers.

blocks.value: 第二段明确指出，当用户登录或提供敏感信息时，攻击者就会窃取数据。
C. When users login or provide sensitive information.
Which is NOT a motive or reason for phishing mentioned in the passage?

choices.label: C. To gain control of someone else's computer network.
D. To attack the dangerous hackers.

blocks.value: 文章列举了身份盗用、控制网络、获取私密邮件和客户记录，没有提到攻击黑客本身。
D. To attack the dangerous hackers.
What is the main idea of Paragraph 4?

choices.label: A. To describe the reasons for phishing attacks.
B. To teach readers how to spot phishing attacks.
C. To help users design their passwords.
D. To tell readers phishing attacks happen every day.

blocks.value: 第四段讲的是如何识别钓鱼网站，比如观察地址栏、从根域名重新登录。
B. To teach readers how to spot phishing attacks.
How can 2FA protect users from phishing attacks?

choices.label: A. Users need two keys to login, and the user can't give away one of the keys.
B. The attacker needs a fingerprint or eyeball scan to access the account.
C. Nobody can log into the account under any circumstances.
D. Two people have to approve the login, so the attacker can't do it alone.

blocks.value: 2FA 需要密码和动态验证码两把钥匙，攻击者即使骗到密码也更难完成登录。
A. Users need two keys to login, and the user can't give away one of the keys.
Which of the following statements is TRUE according to the passage?

choices.label: A. Every phishing attack involves deleting the victim's identity to commit fraud.
B. In a phishing attack, an attacker controls a victim with a stronger computer.
C. You should check your bank account carefully before submitting your data.
D. If a phishing attack is successful, users willingly give attackers sensitive data.

blocks.value: 文中强调攻击者通过伪装和诱导让用户自己提交登录信息和敏感数据。
D. If a phishing attack is successful, users willingly give attackers sensitive data.

Have you ever been in a conversation where the other person wasn't really listening to what you were saying? Maybe they were distracted
about their own response, or just not interested. It is annoying and even discouraging. But active listening is a way to ensure that all parties are heard and understood.
Active listening is a skill that requires focus, patience, and
open mind. Here, we will discuss the basic elements of active listening, techniques to become an active listener, and why it's important in our daily life.
Active listening is a practice that promotes mutual understanding and effective communication. It involves focusing
the speaker and fully comprehending their message. This goes beyond just hearing; it
engagement and attention to detail. By actively listening, we show respect to the speaker and create an environment
open and honest communication can continue smoothly.
Being present is vital when practicing active listening,
it involves being fully engaged in the conversation. Non-verbal clues, such as body language and facial expressions, play a significant

in enhancing active listening by providing context and aiding in the explanation of the speaker's message. Maintaining eye contact demonstrates respect, interest, and attentiveness towards the speaker, while body language can show emotions, attitudes, and intentions that words may not express. Active listening calls for giving undivided attention and avoiding distractions, ensuring that the speaker feels
and heard. By using these basic elements, we can truly connect with others and make effective communication.

These techniques, when practiced, enhance the quality of interactions and strengthen relationships. Adding these techniques to your listening skills can have a great influence on your communication abilities.

Directions: In this part you are required to write a composition entitled My Major in no less than 100 words according to the given Chinese outline.

Write a composition entitled **My Major** in no less than 100 words according to the following Chinese outline:
1. 简单描述你所学的专业；
2. 你选择该专业的原因；
3. 你的努力方向。
作文需覆盖专业介绍、选择原因和今后努力方向三点，语言连贯、结构完整、词数达到要求。

My Major

My major is English. It focuses on language skills, literature, translation and practical communication. Through my courses, I learn how to listen, speak, read and write better, and I also gain a broader understanding of different cultures.

I chose this major because I have always been interested in languages. English is widely used in study, work and international communication, so I believe it can open more doors for my future. I also enjoy expressing ideas clearly and helping others communicate.

In the future, I will work harder on vocabulary, speaking and translation. I hope to build solid professional skills and become a useful person in education, trade or cultural exchange.
